item.description: NASA is restarting a search for commercial missions to reboost or service the Hubble Space Telescope, more than two years after concluding existing options were too risky.

item.title: MDA Space gets initial contract to supply antennas for 66 IRIS² satellites
item.description: Canada’s MDA Space has an initial contract to provide antennas for the first 66 LEO satellites Thales Alenia Space aims to help deliver in 2029 for IRIS², Europe’s planned multi-orbit sovereign broadband network.

item.description: HELSINKI — Two Chinese commercial launch firms have passed key hardware milestones as they move toward inaugural flights of reusable launchers.

item.title: India launches navigation satellite
item.description: India launched a satellite Oct. 30 intended to restore a regional navigation system, provided the satellite avoids the fate of its predecessor.

item.title: DoJ urges federal judge to throw out Ligado’s $50 billion lawsuit
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice has made another push to dismiss Ligado Networks’ roughly $50 billion lawsuit over its derailed wireless network plans, arguing the bankrupt satellite operator’s L-band license does not come with protected property rights.

item.title: America needs a Space Academy for the space age
item.description: The United States is moving its space activity outward, from low Earth orbit to the moon, cislunar space and beyond. Rockets and spacecraft are the visible part of that expansion. The harder problem is people. The country needs leaders who can run an enterprise that grows more complicated every year, and a U.S. Space Academy would help supply them.

item.title: Satellogic and HEO extend non-Earth imaging contract
item.description: Satellogic, a company that operates a constellation of imaging satellites, has signed a new contract with HEO to provide the company with imagery of space objects.

item.title: Landspace tops bid to launch China’s Haolong reusable cargo spaceplane
item.description: HELSINKI — Commercial launch firm Landspace has topped a tender to launch an unidentified spacecraft, understood to be the reusable Haolong spaceplane to serve Tiangong space station.

item.description: NASA officials a nuclear electric propulsion mission is still expected to launch in late 2028, despite limited details about its cost and schedule.

item.title: Former FCC adviser Courtney Reinhard to lead Space Bureau
item.description: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr has appointed former FCC adviser Courtney Reinhard to lead the regulator’s Space Bureau.

item.title: Global Telesat Lightspeed service delayed to mid-2028
item.description: Delayed pathfinder satellites for Telesat’s planned Lightspeed broadband constellation have pushed global service back three months to around the end of the second quarter of 2028, the Canadian operator announced Oct. 29.

item.title: Vietnam signs the Artemis Accords
item.description: Vietnam is the latest country to sign the Artemis Accords, becoming the 78th country to do so in the past six years.

item.title: Rendezvous Robotics raises $20 million for self-assembling spacecraft
item.description: Rendezvous Robotics has closed a $20 million funding round as it prepares for in-space demonstrations of technologies for self-assembling spacecraft.

item.title: Seraphim seeking space startups for more intensive accelerator program
item.description: Space technology investor Seraphim announced a more intensive accelerator program for startups Oct. 29, outlining plans to invest $150,000 in 15 of them annually alongside up to 12 months of mentoring and networking support.

item.title: Virgin Galactic rolls out new suborbital spaceplane
item.description: Virgin Galactic’s newest suborbital spaceplane arrived at the company’s New Mexico spaceport for flight tests as its first commercial flights slip further into 2027.
